blocks.text: As pressure grows, Mata Gujri is shown worrying over the rising danger, while the Guru insists that everything has already been placed into the hands of the Khalsa rather than being secured for household inheritance. (1–4)
The Khalsa is told not to fear reproach or scarcity, and the struggle is framed as one in which disgrace belongs to the slanderers of the Panth rather than to those who endure for it. (5–6)
The page closes with fighting around Anandpur intensifying, as local powers attack, territories shake loose, and the conflict broadens beyond private grievance into a full regional confrontation. (7)
